summary: Grace period mismatch causing API gateway reroute loop and elevated 5xx
description:
Issue summary:
Customer observed a sudden increase in 5xx responses for several routes backed by their Dedicated pool. Errors started after a small configuration change to keepalive pruning in the edge fleet.

Impact:
- ~18% error rate (502/503) for BrightChat's production routes over a 30m window.
- User-facing degraded experience for real-time chat flows.
- Customer on Dedicated tier with SLA; reported latency and failed requests.

Environment:
- Dedicated GPU pool (customer pinned) in us-east-1
- API Gateway fronting multiple streaming and non-streaming routes
- Keepalive pruning change rolled out to a subset of apigw nodes on 2026-03-10 02:04 UTC

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Traffic ramp of small constant requests (20-50 rps) from customer.
2) Gateway accepts connections but starts rerouting requests to healthy-looking upstreams.
3) Upstream runtime frequently returns 502/503 shortly after accept.
4) Gateway retries/fanout logic triggers additional upstream connections causing connection churn and higher error floor.

Observed behaviour:
- Apparent reroute loop: gateway marks upstream as healthy (brief probe) then sends in-flight requests that immediately fail; gateway then amplifies retries to other upstreams creating cascading errors.
- Keepalive pruning on some apigw nodes appears to close idle connections aggressively causing warmup latency on runtime prefetched shards.
- Error types: 502 (bad gateway), 503 (service unavailable), occasional 504 on long streams.

Expected behaviour:
- Gateway should honor a short grace/warmup window before considering a backend healthy/unhealthy and avoid immediate re-routing of in-flight requests.

Key logs/metrics attached (links):
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/edge/apigw-errors?orgId=1&from=2026-03-10T01:30:00Z&to=2026-03-10T03:00:00Z
- SRE traces: trace ids included in comments below

Initial triage summary:
- Timing correlates with keepalive pruning configuration sweep.
- Hypothesis: overly aggressive keepalive pruning triggers transient socket churn; combined with gateway's immediate health flip logic this produces a retry-amplification loop.

Next steps planned:
- Roll back keepalive pruning change on affected apigw subset (in progress).
- Add a short graceful warmup window to gateway health evaluation for this route class (hotfix candidate).
- Coordinate with Dedicated infra team to monitor warmup metrics and upstream error rates after rollback.
comments: 2026-03-10 02:40 UTC - BrightChat support: We're seeing 50% of user messages fail intermittently with 502 from your API. Started ~02:10 UTC after your maintenance window. Please advise. (ticket from customer)

2026-03-10 04:12 UTC - SRE (Markus): Noticed keepalive pruning change deployed to 20% of apigw nodes at 02:04 UTC. Nodes show elevated accept queue churn and increased SYN retries. Hypothesis: accept/connect churn causing runtime warmups to fail quickly and trigger gateway retries. Collecting kernel and runtime logs.

2026-03-10 05:02 UTC - Engineering (Lena Ortiz): Runtime logs show rapid NVML warmup on a subset of shards; short-lived prefetched model copies evicted under connection churn. Suggest rollback of pruning.

2026-03-10 06:00 UTC - Support (Aisha): Customer reports error rate dropping to ~3% after rollback. Continuing to monitor and will coordinate a hotfix for gateway health window.
investigation_notes: Correlated timestamp: 2026-03-10 02:04 UTC (keepalive sweep) -> 02:10 UTC error increase.
Apigw nodes with new pruning config show accept queue depth oscillation and short-lived socket resets in kernel logs (dmesg).
Gateway health checker marked backends healthy based on TCP handshake success then immediately routed in-flight requests while runtime was still loading KV cache / model prefetched shards.
Prefetch/warmup latency distribution for gpt-neox-20b-quant shows 95th percentile spike from ~120ms to ~1.2s on affected runtime shards during the window.
Retry amplification observed: default gateway retry policy retried idempotent requests which amplified load to other warmup-starved backends.
No indications of GPU OOMs or permanent runtime crashes; primarily warmup/latency and connection churn.
Relevant traces: trace-7f5a8d -> shows accept, immediate 502 with runtime deferred KV access log; trace-7f5a9e similar.
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation: rolled back keepalive pruning on affected apigw nodes (completed 2026-03-10 05:40 UTC) which reduced 5xx rate to baseline. Permanent fix plan: apply a 250-500ms warmup grace period to gateway health evaluation for model-prefetch-heavy routes and adjust retry policy to reduce aggressive fanout during warmup. Follow-ups: change scheduled as rollout RFC; SRE to run canary for gateway warmup flag and monitor prefetched shard latencies. Customer notified and satisfied with current drop in errors.
next_steps: Implement gateway warmup grace flag (owner: runtime-gateway team).
Adjust retry/fanout policy for non-idempotent streaming routes (owner: api-gateway).
Schedule a canary rollout of warmup grace with metric thresholds (owner: SRE).
Follow-up postmortem and update runbook: apigw keepalive/pruning interactions with dedicated runtime warmup.
